title: fix(plugin-dashboard): a dimensionless table renders a row of every measure and a dimensionless chart one mark per measure, as the spec states (objectui#11261)
body:
Fixes #11261
Clause-②: no

## What this changes

`DatasetWidget` classified every widget that declares no `dimensions` as a one-number tile (`isMetric = METRIC_TYPES.has(widgetType) || dimensions.length === 0`). So the card's `{ type: 'table', dataset: 'sales', values: ['revenue', 'cost', 'margin'] }` rendered `revenue` alone. Every door accepts that widget, and the spec's own metric-family arity refusal sends authors there. Its ADR-0087 entry `dashboard-widget-metric-family-multi-measure-refused` (`replacement`, read in the installed `@objectstack/spec` 17.5.0) says: "`type: 'table'` renders a row of measures, and the chart families (`bar` / `line` / `area` / `combo`) render one mark per measure".

Per triage `5918660676` (the renderer delivers the stated behaviour; no spec narrowing):

- **Only a metric-family type is a tile by type.** A widget with no dimension stays a tile, unless it carries two or more measures on a type the spec names. Those are `table` / `pivot`, or a widget whose family (`CHART_TYPE_MAP`) is `bar` / `line` / `area` / `combo` (`MEASURE_AXIS_CHART_FAMILIES`).
- **table / pivot:** the existing flat-table branch renders the one row the dimensionless query answers, with every measure as a column. No totals footer is requested or drawn, because that row already IS the `[]` grand-total grouping.
- **bar / line / area / combo:** the single row is transposed into one chart row per declared measure, in declaration order. The category is the measure's `headerLabel` (the widget's one measure-label channel). The value sits under one series labelled with the existing `dashboard.total` key, so no new string is minted. A `compareTo` the widget asks for draws as one overlay series beside each measure. The dimensioned overlay path is byte-identical (same data keys and labels).
- **One measure, no dimension:** unchanged. It takes the metric branch on every type and renders the tile, byte-identical. This is pinned for `table`, `pivot`, `bar`, `line`, `area` and `combo`.
- **Types the spec's text does not name** (`pie`, `donut`, `funnel`, `scatter`, `column`, `horizontal-bar`, `radar`, `treemap`, `sankey`): measured and unchanged. A dimensionless one with two measures is still a tile. It renders `values[0]`, and objectui#8894's warning still names the dropped measure. This goes back as an open question in the report, and no display semantics are invented for these types.
- objectui#8894's warning code is untouched. It follows `isMetric`, so it no longer fires for the widgets that now render every measure. One example in `DatasetWidget.unrenderedMeasures-8894.test.tsx` moved. Its SUBJECT "covers the dimensionless arm" used a dimensionless `bar`, which is no longer a tile, so it now uses a `pie`, which still is. Its assertions are unchanged.

## Pins

`DatasetWidget.dimensionlessMeasures-11261.test.tsx` draws real Recharts marks through the registry, using the `DatasetWidget.chartConfigMarks-9203` harness.

| Row | Kind |
|---|---|
| the card's `table` (and `pivot`) over revenue, cost, margin renders one row with all three, no footer, no warning | SUBJECT |
| a two-measure dimensionless `bar` draws two `.recharts-bar-rectangle`, with category ticks `Revenue`, `Cost` | SUBJECT |
| the same for `combo`; `line` / `area` plot across the two measure labels | SUBJECT |
| a comparison on a dimensionless `bar` draws 4 marks (2 + 2 overlay) | SUBJECT |
| a two-measure `metric` tile with no dimension renders the tile markup and still warns | CONTROL |
| a ONE-measure dimensionless table / pivot / bar / line / area / combo renders the tile markup | CONTROL |
| a dimensionless `table` / `bar` queries exactly `{ dimensions: [], measures: values }` (no `totals`) | CONTROL |
| nine unnamed types stay a tile and warn (measured; the open question) | CONTROL |

PR objectui#8887's two pins stay green: the drop on a metric-type tile, and the no-sub-caption byte-identity (`DatasetWidget.subCaption.test.tsx`).

## Ablation (restore the old `isMetric`)

The fix was committed first. `node ../objectstack/scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` then ran in WRAP mode (the anchor must hit once, the write is verified on disk, and a trap restores it). It replaced the new `isMetric` line with the old one and ran the new file, the objectui#8894 file and the sub-caption file.

- The mutation landed: anchor 1 -> 0, blob `9640acd2abcc` -> `4bf0c16ab58b`.
- **7 failed / 38 passed**: exactly the 7 SUBJECT rows went red. All 18 CONTROL rows, all 8 objectui#8894 rows and all 12 sub-caption rows stayed green.
- Restored: blob == HEAD `9640acd2abcc`, and `git diff HEAD` is empty (re-checked independently).

## Gates (at `7d54b7cfb`)

- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-dashboard/src/`: 155 files passed, 1420 passed / 6 skipped. At base `f61dab169` it was 154 files, 1395 / 6; the difference is the new file's 25.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-dashboard type-check`, with the closure built first by turbo: exit 0. `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --listFiles` includes both touched test files.
- `pnpm exec eslint` on the 3 changed source and test files: 0 errors. The 11 warnings in `DatasetWidget.tsx` are the same 11, under the same rules, as at base. The new file has 0 errors and 0 warnings.
- `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`: exit 0. `node scripts/check-control-bytes.mjs`: exit 0. `pnpm check:new-line-citations`: 0 new citations.
- The changeset is markdown, so `node scripts/markdown-test-inputs.mjs --audit` ran (exit 0), and so did `pnpm exec vitest run scripts/__tests__/` (177 files passed, 2 skipped; 5371 passed).
- Consumers: the four app-shell files that render `DatasetWidget`, plus PR objectui#11257's two door pins (types, app-shell): 6 files, 84 passed.

## Acceptance notes

- Census: every authored multi-measure dashboard widget in objectstack's examples declares a dimension (`git grep` over its `origin/main` at `75519e1c0`). objectui's `examples/` and `apps/` author none. So no shipped example changes rendering.
- Docs: no doc or README stated the old "no dimensions is a tile" rule (`grep` over `content/docs`, the package README and `skills/`), so none became false. The changeset carries the user-facing description.
- Observation, not measured through a door, and not filed (no carrier): `chartType = CHART_TYPE_MAP[widgetType] ?? 'bar'` sends a widget with no `type` and a dimension to a bar chart, while the spec defaults `type` to `metric`. A spec-parsed document always carries a type, so this reaches only an unparsed client draft. This change reads `CHART_TYPE_MAP` without that default, so it adds no path through it.
